Subject: Post-call: connection multiplexing profile & quota ask — PulsePay POC

Hi Aditi — thanks again for a constructive call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we're all aligned: 

What we heard from PulsePay:
- Primary use case: payment confirmation + fraud score enrichment in checkout flow (~80% synchronous, 20% streaming/async)
- Peak concurrency target: ~1,200 parallel requests during Black Friday-like spikes (expected POC target: 200–400 sustained; bursts to 1,200 for short windows)
- Typical request size: 40–120 tokens per call; 95th token length ~200 for longer tickets
- Streaming: ~15% of calls will use streaming responses with an expected 3s average stream duration
- Connection model: backend will use long-lived HTTP/2 connections with multiplexing; want to reuse connections across workers

Redwood asks / proposed data items: 
- Please complete the attached conn_profile_template.xlsx with an hourly QPS distribution and percent streaming by endpoint (helps us recommend exact pooling settings)
- Confirm whether you need per-tenant isolation (Dedicated) or hosted quotas are acceptable for POC
- Any compliance gating (SOC2 evidence) required ahead of POC start

Attachments: conn_profile_template.xlsx (xlsx)

Next steps: 
1) Aditi to return the completed profile by EOD Tue 5/26
2) Ben to run a short connection-profile runbook and propose a conservative quota and burst window by 5/24
3) Laura to draft a provisional rate card for the POC (hosted vs. dedicated options)

I left the pricing/discounting section light so we can price accurately against your real profile. Happy to jump on another 30-min sync if it helps.

Thanks,
– Logan

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear notes. Quick clarifications before we fill the template: 

1) Our backend has ~16 workers per region that maintain ~50 HTTP/2 connections each to external services today; we plan to reuse that model.
2) For POC we prefer hosted (lower procurement friction), but want a break-glass path to Dedicated if performance doesn't meet latency SLOs.
3) Streaming percent is closer to 10% for checkout, but we'll include an endpoint-level split in the spreadsheet.
4) Compliance: SOC2 Type II report is needed for internal procurement — can you share the latest evidence?

One ask on throttling: we cannot tolerate 5xx spikes during short bursts. If the hosted rate limit is static QPS, can Redwood offer a short burst window (e.g., 5x baseline for 2–3 minutes) for checkout peak events? If so, what would that cost/look like for the POC?

We'll aim to get the spreadsheet back by 5/26.

Hi Aditi — Ben (Solutions Eng) here. Thanks for the details — a few technical notes and our initial conservative proposal below.

Technical clarifications: 
- Redwood supports long-lived HTTP/2 and HTTP/3; our hosted endpoints allow multiplexing across connections. We limit parallel in-flight requests per connection to avoid head-of-line blocking; default is 100 parallel streams per HTTP/2 connection.
- Default hosted quota is applied at the API key level in QPS; bursts are allowed via a token-bucket with configurable burst windows on a per-customer basis (not enabled by default, but configurable for POCs).
- Streaming sessions hold a KV cache entry and a reserved slot in the concurrency pool (we count streaming sessions against concurrency).

Initial conservative quota proposal for POC (hosted):
- Baseline sustained: 400 concurrent requests (covers expected sustained load)
- Burst window: allow up to 1,200 concurrent for short windows (2–3 minutes) using a provisional burst token bucket (grace period 72 hours after activation)
- Per-connection recommendation: 50–100 parallel streams per HTTP/2 connection depending on your worker CPU and client multiplexing behavior
- 95th p90 latency SLO target we can support: 120–180ms for text-generation endpoints at this concurrency on hosted; streaming adds ~50–150ms depending on response length

Cost/operational note: Burst windows for hosted POCs are metered and priced as an overage bucket in the provisional ratecard — I’ll pass this to Laura for the commercial side. Dedicated fleet would allow higher sustained concurrency with a predictable commit and lower per-token overage.

Next technical step: please confirm (in the attached sheet) hourly QPS and percent streaming, and whether you can accept a per-connection stream cap of 75 as a starting point. I can run a short benchmark with a test key once we have sample payload sizes.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-v3.pdf

Cheers,
– Ben

> - Burst window: allow up to 1,200 concurrent for short windows (2–3 minutes)
> - Per-connection recommendation: 50–100 parallel streams per HTTP/2 connection

Thanks Ben — that maps well to our expectations. Couple of items from our side: 
- We will test with per-connection stream caps at 64, 128, and 256 on our staging clients to measure head-of-line blocking. Please advise whether Redwood's proxy becomes the bottleneck at higher per-connection stream counts.
- Can Redwood provide a confidence run (10–15 minute soak) that simulates 1,200 parallel requests with 10% streaming so we can validate 95th p95 latency under load? If yes, we need an agreed maintenance window and a test endpoint key.
- Regarding SOC2 evidence: please share the last audit report and a list of controls related to data encryption and retention. Procurement will need that ahead of POC kickoff.

We will populate the spreadsheet and return by your 5/26 deadline.

Thanks — SRE team
PulsePay Inc.

Hi Aditi / SRE team — Laura here. Appreciate the clear asks and the signal on burst behavior. Commercial proposal for the POC (hosted):

1) Technical commitments (temporary POC config):
- Provisional hosted quota: baseline 400 concurrent; burst to 1,200 for 3 minutes, up to 6 times/day during the POC window
- We'll enable a test endpoint and run the soak you requested during pre-agreed windows (Ben will coordinate test key and timing)
- Redwood will cap per-connection streams at 100 by default; we can raise to 128 for the soak run and observe proxy behavior

2) Pricing for POC (30 days):
- Flat onboarding fee waived for pilot customers
- Metered usage at hosted rates per token + burst overage: 20% uplift on token rate that applies only to tokens generated during a burst window
- If PulsePay converts to a Dedicated commit within 90 days of pilot end, Redwood will credit 50% of burst overages against the first month of Dedicated commit

3) Deliverables and timeline:
- Ben to run the soak test (10–15 minutes) and share latency profile within 48 hours of receiving completed spreadsheet
- Logan to coordinate a legal handshake for the POC data processing addendum and share SOC2 evidence (SRE asked for) by EOD 5/26
- Target POC kickoff: week of 6/8 pending procurement sign-off

If that looks good we'll send a short POC statement of work and the test endpoint details.

Best,
